sources.entry: _Tools for static analysis, linters and code quality checkers. Also see awesome-static-analysis._

summary.one_liner: A curated, language-by-language list of static analysis tools, linters, formatters and code quality checkers for many programming languages and config formats.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style link list rather than a tool. It organizes entries by programming language (ABAP through Vim Script, plus WebAssembly) and by an "Other" section covering things like Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, YAML, Markdown and security/SAST. Each entry is a tool name with a one-line description, often noting whether it is proprietary (marked with a copyright symbol), not recommended for new projects, or no longer maintained (warning symbol). Some language sections have a collapsed "Deprecated" subsection. The README states that the project feeds the analysis-tools.dev website, which adds rankings and comments, and it sets contribution criteria for new entries: six months of history, 20 GitHub stars, and more than one human contributor.
use_cases: Finding a linter for a specific programming language
Comparing static analysis tools for C or C++ code
Choosing a security scanner (SAST) for a codebase
Finding a code formatter for Go, Kotlin, Python-adjacent or other languages
Discovering open-source versus commercial code quality tools
Locating tools to check infrastructure or config files like Terraform or YAML
notable: Organized by programming language and config format, with a large Other section
Marks proprietary tools and tools that are unmaintained or archived with symbols
Flags tools the community does not recommend for new projects
Feeds the analysis-tools.dev website, which adds rankings and user comments
caveats: Entries are links and descriptions only; the list does not itself run any analysis
Many entries are proprietary (copyright symbol) or deprecated (warning symbol)
The README is truncated in the provided text, so later sections such as PHP and beyond are not fully covered here
